question: What is the average customer age?

answer_sql:
WITH anchor AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(order_date) AS as_of
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
), aged AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_DIFF('YEAR', c.birth_date, a.as_of) - CASE
      WHEN (
        MONTH(a.as_of) * 100 + DAY(a.as_of)
      ) < (
        MONTH(c.birth_date) * 100 + DAY(c.birth_date)
      )
      THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END AS age
  FROM contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
  CROSS JOIN anchor AS a
)
SELECT
  ROUND(AVG(age), 2) AS average_customer_age
FROM aged

body.value: One figure: 56.8 years (56.80108581769692 before rounding), the mean age of every person on Contoso's customer register — all 104,990 of them — where each person's age is their completed years from their own birth date to 2025-12-31, the date of the newest order in the warehouse. A plain unweighted mean over people, one person one vote, so somebody who has placed four hundred orders counts exactly as much as somebody who has never bought anything. WHAT IS NOT IN IT: no weighting by spend, orders or units, so this is not the average age of a buyer or of a sale — it is the average age of a name on the register. No geography, gender or period cut. No one excluded for want of a birth date, because no one lacks one. And it is not the average age TODAY: at today's date the same 104,990 people average 57.61, because the register has aged ten months since the last order was recorded.
